item.title: Associated primes and v-numbers of integral closures of powers of edge ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $I = I(G)$ be the edge ideal of a finite simple graph $G$. We investigate the relationship between the associated primes and $v$-numbers of powers $I^t$ and their integral closures $\overline{I^t}$. For the third power, we establish the associated prime containment $\operatorname{Ass}(S/\overline{I^3}) \subseteq \operatorname{Ass}(S/I^3)$, which yields $v(I^3) \le v(\overline{I^3})$. In contrast, for $t \ge 4$, we show that $\operatorname{Ass}(S/\overline{I^t})$ and $\operatorname{Ass}(S/I^t)$ are in general incomparable. Furthermore, for every fixed $t \ge 3$ and $r\ge 4$, we construct families of graphs for which the discrepancies $v(\overline{I^t}) - v(I^t)$ and $v(I^r)-v(\overline{I^r})$ are arbitrarily large.
item.dc:creator: Trung Chau, Tai Huy Ha, Thanh Vu

item.title: On perfectoid ideals
item.description: arXiv:2610.31964v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study perfectoid ideals using the reduction modulo $p$ of perfectoid rings. We show that perfectoid ideals correspond to ideals in the reduction modulo $p$ on which Frobenius is surjective. We establish the existence of universal $p$-adic power series whose evaluations, together with their compatible $p$-power roots, generate perfectoidizations of ideals. In the special case of the perfectoidization of $\mathbb{Z}_p^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/p^{\infty}}\rangle/(t-1)$, we describe a linear algebra algorithm for computing finite approximations of such generators. We illustrate this by an explicit approximation modulo $8$ of an element $\sigma\in (t-1)_{\mathrm{perfd}}\subseteq \mathbb{Z}_2^{\mathrm{cycl}}\langle t^{1/2^{\infty}}\rangle$ which admits compatible sequences of $2$-power roots and satisfies $\sigma\equiv t-1\pmod{2}$.
item.dc:creator: L\'eo Navarro Chafloque

item.title: Contributions to the Stable Derived Categories of Gorenstein Rings
item.description: arXiv:2610.32074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The stable derived category $D_{sg}(R)$ of a Gorenstein ring $R$ is the Verdier quotient of the bounded derived category $D^b(\mathsf{mod}\, R)$ by the thick subcategory of perfect complexes, and was introduced by Buchweitz as a homological measure of the singularities of $R$. This thesis contributes to its study, centered around representation-theoretic and Koszul duality aspects. In Part I, we complete (over $\mathbb{C}$) the classification of homogeneous complete intersection isolated singularities $R$ for which $D^{\mathbb{Z}}_{sg}(R)$ (respectively, $D^b(\mathsf{coh}\, X)$ for $X = \mathsf{proj}\, R$) contains a tilting object. We then use results of Buchweitz-Iyama-Yamaura to describe the indecomposable objects in $D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R_Y)$ for $R_Y$ the coordinate rings of $4$ points on $\mathbb{P}^1$ and $4$ points on $\mathbb{P}^2$ in general position, and classify their Betti tables. In Part II, for $R$ a Koszul Gorenstein algebra, we study a natural pair of subcategories whose intersection $\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{lin}}(R) \subseteq D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R)$ consists of modules with eventually linear projective resolutions. We prove that such a pair forms a bounded t-structure if and only if $R$ is absolutely Koszul in the sense of Herzog-Iyengar, in which case $D^b(\mathcal{H}^{\mathsf{lin}}(R)) \cong D_{sg}^{\mathbb{Z}}(R)$. We then relate the heart to modules over the Koszul dual $R^!$. This extends the BGG correspondence to any pair of Koszul dual algebras $(R, R^!)$ with $R$ absolutely Koszul Gorenstein, applying e.g. to elliptic normal curves and del Pezzo surfaces of degree $\geq 4$. Finally, we relate our results to conjectures of Bondal and Minamoto on the graded coherence of AS-regular algebras and higher preprojective algebras; we characterise when these conjectures hold in a restricted setting, and give counterexamples to both in all dimensions $\geq 4$.
item.dc:creator: Vincent G\'elinas

item.title: Divisorial ideals and $v$-class semigroups of strictly closed domains
item.description: arXiv:2610.32134v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study divisorial ideals and the $v$-class semigroup of a Noetherian domain satisfying Serre's condition $(S_2)$. We prove that strict closedness is equivalent to Clifford $v$-regularity and describe the structure of the associated $v$-class semigroup. We use these results to characterize finite generation of the class semigroup and Boole $v$-regularity. We also construct prime ideal decompositions of integrally closed divisorial ideals and clarify the relationship between these decompositions and local Boole $v$-regularity. Finally, we study polynomial extensions and use them to construct Boole $v$-regular and locally Boole $v$-regular domains in arbitrary dimension.
item.dc:creator: Ryotaro Isobe

item.title: Noetherian local rings without perfectoid towers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32577v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$. We prove that if a $p$-torsionfree ring $R$, defined by homogeneous equations over $W(k)$, admits a perfectoid tower arising from $(R,(p))$, then its special fiber is $F$-liftable. We also give explicit examples admitting no such tower, including examples with $F$-liftable special fibers.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuki Yamaguchi

item.title: Rank identifications in join-meet ideals of thin distributive lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.32647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L$ be a thin distributive lattice of rank $m+1$, and let $I_L$ be its join-meet ideal in the polynomial ring $S_L$. For $A\subseteq\{1,\dots,m\}$, let $J_A$ be the ideal obtained from $I_L$ by identifying, for every $i\in A$, the variables of the two elements of $L$ of rank $i$. We prove that $J_A$ is prime if and only if $A$ contains no turning rank and does not contain both ranks adjacent to a turning rank. In this case, $S_L/J_A$ is the toric ring obtained from Hibi's parametrization of the Hibi ring of $L$ by identifying suitable pairs of variables, and for an arbitrary $A$ we describe the saturation of $J_A$ as a lattice ideal.
item.dc:creator: Takayuki Hibi, Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi

item.title: Jacobian layers and higher Milnor sequences: rigidity, stabilization, and log-concavity
item.description: arXiv:2610.32523v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f$ be an isolated hypersurface singularity and let $J(f)$ be its Jacobian ideal. We study the higher Milnor numbers $\mu_k(f)=\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_n/\mathfrak m^kJ(f).$ Our main result concerns an ordinary semi-homogeneous singularity $f=f_r+f_{r+1}+\cdots$, where the projective hypersurface defined by $f_r$ is smooth. We prove that $\mu_k(f)=\mu_k(f_r) \qquad\text{for every }k\geq0.$ This gives the equal-weight case of a conjecture of Shi, Yau, and Zuo. The main algebraic input is the common-order case of the Valabrega--Valla criterion. From it, we obtain the graded Jacobian module and the exact intersection formula. As a consequence, we obtain a closed formula for $\mu_k$ and determine the sharp stabilization index of $\mathfrak m^kJ(f)$. We also determine the optimal uniform range in which the Tjurina formula holds for all ordinary semi-homogeneous germs with fixed $n$ and $r$. We next consider the log-concavity property. For ordinary semi-homogeneous singularities, the higher Milnor sequence has an initial log-convex part and a log-concave tail. For an arbitrary isolated hypersurface singularity in $n\geq2$ variables, both the higher Milnor and higher Tjurina sequences are eventually strictly log-concave. In the plane curve case, we prove that the log-concavity defects change sign at most once, and we characterize the sequences which are log-concave at every positive index. Finally, we give examples showing that the higher Milnor sequence does not determine the contact-equivalence class.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwen Liu, Stephen S. -T. Yau, Mingyi Zhang

item.title: Ideal transition systems
item.description: arXiv:2412.17320v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study an inductive method of computing initial ideals and Gr\"obner bases for families of ideals in a polynomial ring. This method starts from a given set of pairs $(I,J)$ where $I$ is any ideal and $J$ is a monomial ideal contained in the initial ideal of $I$. These containments become a system of equalities if one can establish a particular transition recurrence among the chosen ideals. We describe explicit constructions of such systems in two motivating cases -- namely, for the ideals of matrix Schubert varieties and their skew-symmetric analogues. Despite many formal similarities with these examples, for the symmetric versions of matrix Schubert varieties, it is an open problem to construct the same kind of transition system. We present several conjectures that would follow from such a construction, while also discussing the special obstructions arising in the symmetric case.
item.dc:creator: Eric Marberg, Brendan Pawlowski

item.title: A note on the class of sober rings
item.description: arXiv:2507.15978v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study sober rings, a class of commutative rings in which every prime non-maximal ideal is not the intersection of the prime ideals strictly containing it. We establish basic structural properties of sober rings and investigate connections to other known classes of rings. We show that sobriety is preserved under quotients and localizations and we examine the behavior of sobriety for polynomial extensions.
item.dc:creator: Saeid Jafari, Ernesto Lax

item.title: Comparing the face rings of a boolean complex and its barycentric subdivision
item.description: arXiv:2507.20037v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the relationship between the Stanley--Reisner ring (a.k.a. face ring) of a simplicial or boolean complex $\Delta$ and that of its barycentric subdivision. These rings share a distinguished parameter subring. S. Murai asked if they are isomorphic, equivariantly with respect to the automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)$, as modules over this parameter subring. We show that, in general, the answer is no, but for Cohen--Macaulay complexes in characteristic coprime to $|\operatorname{Aut}(\Delta)|$, it is yes, and we give an explicit construction of an isomorphism. To give this construction, we adapt a pair of tools introduced by A. Garsia in 1980. The first one transfers bases from a Stanley--Reisner ring to closely related rings of which it is a Gr\"obner degeneration, and the second identifies bases to transfer.
item.dc:creator: Ben Blum-Smith, Sophie Marques

item.title: Spherical Completeness, Coherence, and GCD Properties of Formal Power Series and Witt Vector Rings
item.description: arXiv:2608.04897v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $K$ be a complete nonarchimedean valued field with $v(K^\times)=\mathbf R$, and let $V=\mathcal O_K$. We prove that $K$ is spherically complete if and only if $V[[T]]$ is coherent, and that this is also equivalent to $V[[T]]$ being a GCD domain. If $K$ is perfect of characteristic $p$, the same characterization holds for the Witt vector ring $W(V)$. Thus, this settles the previously unresolved full-real-value-group case in the coherence problems for both formal power series and Witt vector rings. In particular, this result also gives affirmative answers to Questions~9 and~10 of Anderson--Kang--Park. The proof combines a coherence criterion for complete rings with a spherically complete valuation quotient and a uniform construction of non-finitely generated intersections of two principal ideals from an empty ball chain.
item.dc:creator: Yiding Wang

item.title: Palindromic switching rook polynomials and domino-stable collections of cells
item.description: arXiv:2511.13982v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a finite collection of cells. Two non-attacking rook configurations on $\mathcal{P}$ are switching-equivalent if one can be obtained from the other by a sequence of switches inside rectangles contained in $\mathcal{P}$. The switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ enumerates the resulting equivalence classes according to the number of rooks. We characterize the collections of cells whose switching rook polynomial is palindromic. More precisely, we introduce a new combinatorial property, called domino-stability, and we prove that the switching rook polynomial of $\mathcal{P}$ is palindromic if and only if $\mathcal{P}$ is domino-stable.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Navarra, Ayesha Asloob Qureshi, Giancarlo Rinaldo

item.title: Stack Constructions and Equality Cases for Laffey's Bound for Maximal Commutative Matrix Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2605.01387v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study equality cases in Laffey's lower bound for local maximal commutative subalgebras of matrix algebras with cube-zero radical. We introduce a stacking operation that combines algebras with common outer Loewy layers while preserving maximal commutativity. This yields standard equality bricks $B_{a,c}=(a,ac+1,c;a+c)$ for all $a,c\ge2$ and reduces further constructions to smaller building blocks. We establish the existence of all minimal equality bricks on the balanced branch and obtain sharp realizations throughout the $(4,5)$-sector. We also construct the first nontrivial nearly balanced root over arbitrary fields. We determine the balanced--nearly-balanced envelope of the numerical Laffey profile and give an arithmetic criterion for preservation of sharpness under stacking. As a consequence, the profile is attained in every matrix dimension $14\le n\le52$ and $93\le n\le114$, as well as along five infinite families over arbitrary fields. The main existence and interval results are proved in characteristic zero; the field-independent constructions are stated explicitly.
item.dc:creator: Ma{\l}gorzata Nowak-K\k{e}pczyk

item.title: Bounds on the F-Pure Threshold of Isolated Hypersurface Singularities
item.description: arXiv:2606.04014v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain bounds for the $F$-pure threshold of isolated hypersurface singularities over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic $p$ in terms of classical singularity invariants. For an irreducible plane curve whose value semigroup has first two generators $\beta_0,\beta_1$, we show that the $F$-pure threshold is at most $\frac{1}{\beta_0}+\frac{1}{\beta_1}$ and differs from it by less than $\frac{1}{\gcd(\beta_0,\beta_1)p}$, with equality when certain base-$p$ digits add without carrying, and we give an example showing that higher weighted-order terms can change the $F$-pure threshold. We also conjecture a lower bound in terms of the Milnor number, and prove it for semi-quasi-homogeneous singularities, for all plane curves, and whenever the number of variables exceeds $p$. In particular, it holds in characteristic $2$. As applications, we reprove Igusa's formula for the log canonical threshold of a complex plane branch (with integer coefficients), prove the conjecture of Musta\c{t}\u{a}, Takagi and Watanabe for such branches, and bound the log canonical threshold of complex isolated hypersurface singularities.
item.dc:creator: Yotam Svoray

item.title: Commutative coherent rings with $\mathcal{GP}\not\subseteq\mathcal{GF}$
item.description: arXiv:2608.17748v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every field $k$, we construct a commutative coherent $k$-algebra admitting a Gorenstein projective module that is not Gorenstein flat.
item.dc:creator: Chencheng Zhang
